0.label: plaited_band_base
0.description: A horizontal band of three-strand plait closing the bottom of the plank's frame.
0.iconography: The lower edge of the woven frame that encloses the three figures; plait as binding and enclosure.

1.label: plaited_band_top
1.description: A horizontal band of plait closing the top of the frame, below the plank's uncarved upper end.
1.iconography: The upper edge of the same woven frame (see #0).

2.label: crowned_figure_mudfish_legs
2.description: The lowest of three stacked figures in the central channel: a square head under a crown of pointed triangles, fists raised with objects, and legs drawn as two long loops meeting in a 'W'.
2.iconography: The pointed crown marks a king (adé). Looped legs recall the mudfish-legged ruler of Olókun and Benin imagery — a sign of divine kingship. In a chronicle reading, one ruler in a sequence of three.

3.label: plaited_side_band
3.description: The long left-hand band of plait running the full height between the top and bottom bands.
3.iconography: Left side of the woven frame; one continuous border split by the detector from #5.

4.label: crowned_figure_with_staffs
4.description: The top figure of the three: a square head under a zigzag-banded crown, a short staff in each hand, legs outlined in a long inverted 'V'.
4.iconography: A crowned person holding two staffs — a ruler with emblems of office, heading the column.

5.label: plaited_side_band
5.description: The long right-hand band of plait, mirror of #3.
5.iconography: Right side of the woven frame.

6.label: figure_with_round_head
6.description: The middle figure: a head inside a round outline (a cap, halo or mask), fists holding objects, a striated lower body.
6.iconography: Unlike the two crowned figures, this one wears a round head-covering — perhaps a different office, a priest, or a ruler shown differently. Its place between two crowns keeps it within the sequence.

panel.title: Ife plank: three crowned figures in a woven frame
panel.object_type: carved plank (door leaf or post face)
panel.summary: A tall plank whose carving is a frame of plait on all four sides enclosing a channel with three frontal figures stacked one above the other. Two of the three wear pointed or zigzag crowns and hold objects in both hands.

register_readings.reading: Between two full-height plait bands: a crowned figure with staffs (#4), a figure in a round cap (#6), and a crowned figure with looped legs (#2).

panel.composition: Frame-and-file: a closed woven border around a single column of three figures of similar size, spaced evenly on the axis.
panel.narrative: Three crowned or capped rulers, one above another, held inside an unbroken woven frame, is the closest thing in the collection to a king list: a line of succession presented as equal, repeated authority. The frame's continuity would suit a lineage. Which rulers, if any, cannot be said from the carving; Ife's own list of Ọọ̀ni is the obvious oral source to test it against.
panel.hypotheses: Supports 'chronicle' more directly than any tray: a vertical sequence of crowned figures. Weakly relevant to 'pattern as number' (three figures; the plait is not obviously counted).
cross_panel_links: EBA-Div_00312_panel_01 repeats the same frame-and-three-figures scheme.
The looped legs of #2 compare with the displayed figure on EBA-Div_00311_panel_00 (#5).
uncertainties: The crowns could be crested coiffures; the photograph is soft.
The side bands #3 and #5 are one frame split into boxes, not motifs.
